My role is not to make a formal conclusion as to the precise extent of the contributory negligence but to take into account whether or not the Claimant was probably guilty of contributory negligence, the likely extent and whether or not as much as 50%, in coming to a view as to whether or not the proposed settlement is appropriate and whether or not it should be approved. [para 131] Finds driver bore higher responsibility for failing proper lookout, key liability reasoning under s 5R. 131. Although under the current caselaw, the fact that the injured person is a pedestrian no longer has the significance that it used to, the evidence suggests that there was a significantly higher degree of responsibility for the cause of the accident on the part of the driver than that of the pedestrian. The driver certainly did not keep a proper lookout and, indeed, did not observe the pedestrian or keep a lookout in her direction at all. [para 141] Indicates likely contributory negligence at about 15% rather than 50%. 141. response.criterion: The sorter appears to have been responding to the presence or absence of entitlement to non-economic loss (NEL) based on whole person impairment (WPI) assessments.

groups.description: Documents where claimants are entitled to non-economic loss due to a whole person impairment (WPI) greater than 10%.
distinguishing_features: Entitlement to non-economic loss due to WPI > 10%

groups.description: Documents where claimants are entitled to non-economic loss, but the WPI is not explicitly stated as greater than 10%, or the entitlement is based on other factors such as age or specific injuries.
distinguishing_features: Entitlement to non-economic loss without explicit WPI > 10%

groups.description: Documents where claimants are not entitled to non-economic loss, often due to a WPI assessment of less than 10%.
distinguishing_features: No entitlement to non-economic loss due to WPI < 10%

response.notes: The sorting criterion is based on the entitlement to non-economic loss, which is often linked to the whole person impairment percentage.
